status: partial prepared implementation; not published or versioned as 1.72
finding: Generic world-event callbacks created one goroutine per send to an unbuffered hub channel. A slow hub could retain arbitrarily many visual forwarding goroutines; periodic time/event loops also blocked on that channel.
implementation: Direct non-blocking transient enqueue, ordinary capacity1024 and independently reserved encounter capacity128. Telegraph, raid-phase and crystal-repair notices do not share ordinary visual capacity.

Each staged payload is at most16KiB and scene ID256bytes; bytes are copied for immutable ownership. Unknown/private reply types, invalid sizes, stopping state and full/unavailable queues are rejected without a waiting goroutine or world-lock block.
All generic main world broadcast producers and periodic time/public-event producers use the bounded enqueue. Private quest, reward, wallet, inventory, save and combo paths remain separate.
The existing hub select services both lanes plus registration, retirement and shutdown. This is reserved encounter space, not guaranteed strict priority scheduling.

Healthz retains release/database/runtime fields and adds queue lengths/capacities plus ordinary, encounter and invalid drop counters. No message bodies, credentials or account names are logged or exposed by these counters.

verification.negative: Full ordinary and encounter queues reject immediately; unknown wallet_update, empty/oversized payload and oversized scene metadata do not enter presentation lanes. Stopping/nil queue paths do not block.
verification.positive: A full ordinary queue still admits a telegraph to the reserved lane with captured scene/body intact; normal enqueue recovers after drain; caller byte mutation cannot change queued data; exact size boundaries are accepted.
verification.concurrency: 64 synthetic producers make512 attempts into an owned8-slot lane with no consumer: exactly8 are retained and504 are counted as dropped. No throughput/player capacity is inferred.
verification.compatibility: Actual health response matches queue metrics while retaining readiness; existing health, scene-delivery, telegraph and shutdown admission groups passed. Source call-site review found no remaining direct generic broadcast sends outside the queue helper.

limits: Queues can drop transient presentation under overload. Encounter drops can lose warnings and must be treated as failed operational readiness; reserved space does not prove sufficient real encounter/player capacity.
These are isolated enqueue, production-delivery and handler checks, not a full runHub scheduling proof, fresh production binary, real browser/socket encounter, campaign or capacity soak.

Other asynchronous private workers, same-scene visibility/interest, jump policy, connected route compatibility and remaining security/operations gates still require completion before milestone closure.
No production services, accounts, saves, wallets or host configuration were changed. Ordered predecessors and exact-source CI/public acceptance still precede1.72 publication.
